expectations.criterion: [MANDATORY] attributes the growth to decoded image size via the image cache or memory profiler before changing code
expectations.evidence: Step 1, 'Confirm the cause first', comes before any code change. It uses imageCache.currentSizeBytes, liveImageCount and pendingImageCount, plus DevTools Memory snapshots, to compare decoded dimensions with on-screen size. It sets explicit criteria for telling 'full-res decoding confirmed' apart from 'real leak', and the fix in step 2 is conditioned on that result ('If full-res decoding is confirmed...').

expectations.criterion: sets cacheWidth/cacheHeight (or an equivalent resize) to the display size instead of the source resolution
expectations.evidence: Step 2 computes px = constraints.maxWidth * devicePixelRatio and passes cacheWidth: px to Image.network. It also names the memCacheWidth/memCacheHeight equivalents for cached_network_image and ResizeImage for custom providers.

expectations.criterion: rejects periodically clearing the whole image cache as the fix
expectations.evidence: The opening states that clearing the cache 'would likely mask the problem rather than fix it, and it adds re-decode jank'. Step 3 limits clearing to an optional OS memory-pressure 'safety net only' and says 'Don't clear the cache on every scroll'. It prefers bounding maximumSizeBytes instead.

expectations.criterion: verifies bounded memory after the resize with the same repeated scroll flow
expectations.evidence: Step 4: 'Repeat the exact scenario from step 1 and report the before/after numbers: peak and steady memory, currentSizeBytes, and frame times, as ranges across several runs.' Step 1 defines the flow as the same grid, dataset and scroll pattern (top to bottom and back three times), and the expected outcome as a plateau near the cache limit.

judgment.summary: The response meets all four criteria. It diagnoses before changing code, using imageCache metrics and DevTools snapshots to attribute growth to oversized decodes and to separate that from a true leak. It fixes the problem by decoding at display size with a DPR-aware cacheWidth, and it rejects cache clearing as the fix, keeping it only as an optional OS-pressure safety net. It verifies by rerunning the identical scroll scenario and comparing before/after memory. The one minor weakness is that it still provides clear-on-pressure code, which some reviewers might see as partly accommodating the original request, but it is clearly framed as secondary.
